utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we begin today, there's a matter I'd like to deal with. The Chamber refers to the accused's motion for revision of trial transcripts filed on the 27th of May, 2013, in which the accused requests that the Chamber order the Tribunal's language section to listen to the audio recordings of all B/C/S-speaking witnesses in his case and, together with the court reporters, produce an accurate revised transcript of this testimony. The Chamber would like to hear from the Registry on this issue, and therefore invites the Registry to file a response to the motion pursuant to Rule 33 of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This response should be filed by the close of business on the 10th of June. Should the Prosecution wish to respond to the motion, it should do so by the same date. In addition, the Chamber notes that in support of the relief sought in the motion, the accused refers to the Chamber's recent order of 14th of May, 2013, that all so-called draft translations of witness statements of Defence witnesses be revised by the CLSS. In that respect, the Chamber notes that on the 22nd of May, 2013, the accused filed a report on the progress of this exercise in which he states, in paragraph 2, that contrary to the Chamber's impression he and his team never requested draft translations from the CLSS and that the decision to provide such translations was made by the CLSS. Accordingly, the Chamber considers that the Rule 33 submission which is to be filed by the 10th of June should also address paragraph 2 of the accused's report on draft translation of witness statements, filed on the 22nd of May, 2013. In doing so, the Registry should provide a short description of its procedure for translation requests and shall also address the issue of the specific 59 draft translations referred to in the accused's report, including how they came to be draft rather than fully revised translations. As for the hearing for today, I take it the parties have been informed of the revised sitting schedule? Very well. Then please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to focus your attention on your incident report -- actually, your report about incident 7 and please tell us what was said about that incident and what the physical evidence showed.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This incident happened on the 25th of May, 1994. According to the indictment, a projectile fired from infantry weapons hit a bus at the intersection of Nikole Demonje Street and the former Avnoj boulevard. Now it's called Branilaca Dobrinje, I believe. According to the indictment, the projectile was fired from the direction of the theological faculty at Nedzarici. We visited the site and went to that faculty at Nedzarici and found out that there is no line of sight between that place and the site of the incident. We were also able to show that based on the altitude of the Faculty of Theology and the site of the incident. The Faculty of Theology has a lower altitude and between that facility and the incident site there are also some houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please repeat the question and do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please put a pause between the question and answers. Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked image 68 from page 104 from document 1D7902 to be put on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please comment on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows that the distance between the Faculty of Theology and the incident site is 1.527 metres, which is a substantial instance, whereas a machine-gun is used up to a distance of 1.500 metres and a sniper rifle up to 1.200 metres. In other words, the distance is greater than that at which a machine-gun can be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you choose the Faculty Of Theology, given the fact that the OTP is not sure that the projectile was fired from there?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Faculty of Theology is often mentioned as the place from which the projectile was fired. All other buildings are at a lower altitude, all other buildings surrounding it, so that it's not possible for the projectile to be -- to have been fired from any other nearby building. There are other houses between that place and the bus, but the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please start over with the answer. The interpreter cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Interpreters were not able to follow. Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that you said [In English] "so that it's not possible for the projectile to be -- to have been fired from any other nearby building. There are other houses between ..." and so on --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, he's read the transcript where it was stopped. So if you could repeat from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat the part about the other end of the street relative to the bus. From that direction no projectile could have been fired from the positions of the VRS because the separation line at the end of that street was moved 200 to 250 metres toward the Faculty of Theology, which was confirmed by the commander of the Dobrinja Brigade, General Ismet Hadzic. Moreover, somewhere halfway down the street there was a barrier that blocked the line of sight toward the bus. That barrier was placed in front of the Dobrinja Brigade command and it was a standard way of protecting commands in Sarajevo. I was able to see some photographs of the command of the 105th Motorised Brigade at Trampina Street where it was also impossible to snipe because there were protective barriers, which is normal in war time. So there was a Dobrinja Brigade command and there must have been armed BH army soldiers securing the facility. It's almost certain. There is another piece of information that rules out the possibility of the fire -- of the bullet to have been fired from the positions of the VRS around the Faculty of Theology because a bullet fired from infantry weapons from this distance would have had about 90 per cent less energy than the amount it would have had at a distance of a hundred metres. According to the reports, the bullet first hit the tire then ricochetted, pierced the panelling of the bus, and then wounded two women. After the ricochet, the bullet additionally loses some 30 per cent of its energy at least and it is certain that it wouldn't have had enough energy to pierce both the metal panelling of the bus and continue its trajectory to wound one woman and then another at the other end of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you -- or do finish.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on all these facts, it is fully certain that in this case the bullet that hit the bus was not fired from the positions of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now get image 69 on page 105. [In English] Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what this image shows.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows the terrain profile along this line from the Faculty of Theology to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can also see that the Faculty of Theology is at a lower altitude than the incident site marked F7 here and if we take into account the height of the faculty building of some 15 metres, then the spot where there were some firing positions at the Faculty of Theology - and there were, we ascertained that - through the courtesy of the faculty staff we got some photographs that they made after the end of the war and it is clear that there were some firing positions, but it was impossible to see the incident site from there. Since there are other houses there, the line of sight is completely blocked.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see image 67 and 67a, page 103 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Poparic, I couldn't read the letters which is inside the small black boxes in the image 69.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, in the profile. This is -- these are some Google markings. They only show the spot where incident F-7 took place. This is -- this profile is a bit longer than 1.500 metres. The spot marked F-7 on the upper line was lowered down on this scale here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What does number 614 represent, if that's 614 in the middle of that graph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll leave it at that. We can zoom in with the computer --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or I can explain. When we make such a profile, it has a sliding scale that enables you to read the exact values. It shows the altitude and so on. This hasn't really anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to do with this. This is what Google gives you automatically and it can be moved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Further to the right. In the upper part do you see the small black box 614v? Shall we zoom in further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the altitude of that spot, as given by Google. You can move this to the left or right and get the altitude for any spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why that place? Why that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's picked at random. It doesn't matter. I could have moved it to the end --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but the altitude doesn't matter to me. It's only this profile that matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In what relation with regard to the projection is the incident site to this altitude of 614?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The yellow arrow indicates the incident site, so it's higher up than 614 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get image 67 and image 67a on page 103.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the faculty is oriented, the direction it's facing?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not facing the site of the incident, but this terrace here -- well, there are no weapons nests here. So if we look at 67a, it was taken in the direction towards the incident site, so the terrace is roughly at the level of these gun holes and the gun holes are roughly 90 degrees in the other direction, roughly towards Alipasino Polje and to the east if we are speaking in geographical terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who mentioned the Faculty of Theology as the source of fire?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was mentioned by expert Weijden, it was mentioned by this witness, that it came from there. There are perhaps some other documents. I think the police established that it came from the direction of the Faculty of Theology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The other Serb positions, the other Serb positions that were closer, was there visibility and could it have --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. As we see in image 66, this is the area with these houses that are roughly the same height. So if we take into account that from this house that can be seen in the back, there was another 250 metres approximately to the line of separation, it is absolutely impossible I mean to have targeted from there. Otherwise, a building could have been seen from which one could fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please focus on incident number 8. Could you please briefly tell us what is claimed in relation to this incident and what your expertise established.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the incident of the 19th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's page 108 in Serbian and it's paragraph 112 in English. Please go on. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is claimed is that a bullet was fired from a side-arm and wounded several persons. It was fired on a tram and it is claimed that the fire came from the Jewish cemetery, from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. On the basis of photo documentation, it was very easy to establish that the bullet had not been fired from the direction of the Jewish cemetery and that can clearly be seen if one looks at the place where the bullet hit the panelling of the tram and where it exited. There is a major difference in terms of height and also in terms of direction. A bullet that would have been fired from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, the Jewish cemetery, would have hit the tram under an angle that is very close to 90 degrees. But the angle of descent would be a few degrees, 5 or 6 degrees. Now, what does that mean? That means that in that case the place where the projectile entered the panelling would be 2 or 3 centimetres above the point where it exited in terms of height, and in terms of direction it would almost be in the same place, or rather, it could have been moved a few centimetres in relation to the point of entry. On the basis of photo documentation, it was established what the point of entry and the point of exit of the projectile was - there is a major difference there. Obviously the tram had been hit from a direction which is opposite to the direction in which the tram was moving. At a small angle in relation to the horizontal plain, or rather, in relation to the axis of the tram on the horizontal plain and on the vertical plain the angle of descent was very large.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 78 on page 116, could you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 78 we see the incident site, that is point F8. Direction 2 is the approximate position of the Army of Republika Srpska by the Jewish cemetery and direction 1 is the approximate direction showing where the bullet had been fired from. And this direction was established and confirmed also on the basis of the opening at the entry point. It was a high-quality photograph and it was possible to establish what the direction was on the basis of the profile of this opening at the point of entry. It just confirmed that obvious fact that was shown in image 76, where one can see the point where the projectile entered the panelling.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have image 76.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On this image we see the point that is circled on the left-hand side. That is the point where the projectile entered the panelling and the police marked that with this white arrow. This other point down here is one that we marked on the basis of the photograph, I don't know if we provided it -- yes, photograph 75. It shows the point of exit on the tram panelling, and this is the approximate position as far as we could assess, but there is no major error there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the external panelling of this tram, can you mark the point of exit from the panelling where this impact was?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's mark it with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see image -- I beg your pardon. Can you initial this and could you please put the date there as well.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the 30th today, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3637, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now please have photograph 71a, it's on page 110 within paragraph 117 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what can be seen in this image?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This image shows the trace of the bullet that passed through the panelling of the tram and it hit the railing of the chair. This image can be useful for us because it shows that the bullet had considerable energy and that indicates that it had been fired from a relatively short range because it had to pierce two panelings on the tram which is rather thick, and that decreases energy. And then it still had the energy to cause this damage in this metal railing of the chair. So we see that the impact is very strong. It almost pierced it. That indicates the high energy of the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who marked these two arrows?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the police that marked this. This is from the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether they mark only the point of impact or also the direction?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, well, once the bullet got through the panelling it hit this chair and then -- I think it's on the other side, and then it fell and it's marked on the right-hand side with a number 1. The police noted that and it was 7.9 millimetres. That's what they believed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the blue circle on the left-hand photograph, what does that show?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue circle on the left-hand photograph shows some damage that I did not manage to decipher on the basis of this photograph. They measured something, some distance, but the chair is on the other side. So it is not of any relevance in terms of determining the direction. These photographs just show roughly that this bullet had a high degree of energy and this shows that it was fired from a relatively short range and that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no doubt that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Interpreters didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was: What was your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion is that the bullet was fired from the Executive Council building. We could not establish the exact height and the position within the building itself because of the relatively small image, so it is only natural that there are some errors. But undeniably all these traces show that this had been fired from the building of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now deal with incident F9 on page 117 in the Serbian version and the paragraph number is 126. Again, I'm kindly asking you to explain what the physical evidence shows and how this incident was portrayed.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of June, 1994, the street of Djure Jaksica, Sanela Muratovic was shot in the shoulder. It was an exit/entry wound. It is claimed that a projectile was fired from the direction of the Institute for the Blind that is about 100-something metres away from the site of this incident. There is very little information about the incident itself. Everything is based on the testimony of one person who was next to Sanela Muratovic, the wounded person. In her statements there are two versions. According to one version that the OTP presented, the two of them were standing by a trench next to the building in Djure Jaksica number 17. There is a line of sight, there is optical visibility from there towards the Institute for the Blind, but only the upper part of the window can be seen and it's rather big. It's about 3 metres, which indicates that if the marksman was there he had to be at some height, so practically towards the top of that room in order to be able to target this position. Since there is a relatively short distance between this building and -- well, I find this highly improbable, although I cannot say that with any degree of certainty because the marksman would have been exposed to great danger. He could easily have been hit with an Osa Zolja rifle grenade and so on and it doesn't seem logical to me that that would have been a sniper position. This building is often referred to in various statements as a source of sniper fire, but I did not find any documents that would indicate that there was indeed -- I mean a photograph, a film, that there really was something there that would indicate that that used to be a sniper position. On the assumption that the bullet had been fired from this institute, Sanela Muratovic would have been hit in the front part of the shoulder as described by this witness and the exit wound would be towards the left. The angle could have been about 5 or 6 degrees. Unfortunately, there is no medical documentation that says anything about the nature of this wound except for it being an exit/entry wound. So that's the only thing that we know, that it was an exit/entry wound. Now, where the entry was, where the exit was, what the direction was, we don't have any information about that. Another version of Medina Omerovic's was that she and Sanela Muratovic were in the street of Djure Jaksica and that soldiers cautioned them that they should hurry because sniper fire was starting. They started running and at that moment a gun-shot was heard and Sanela was hit. Then they ran to the trench where the soldiers gave them aid. So if this version is correct then Sanela was hit in Djure Jaksica Street and then she ran to that trench. However, if it's in Djure Jaksica, then the view from this place at the Institute for the Blind is such that they probably could not have been seen in that place. There is no information that it was on the front side of the institute, I mean that there was some kind of opening or something through which they could have been seen there. So practically what we have here is very scant information on the basis of which we could establish where fire had been opened from. We can only establish what an entry/exit wound would look like if she had been hit from one place or another, but I don't find that to be very useful. There is a basic document, that is the medical report on the wound itself, and in cases of wounding with small arms fire that is of crucial importance. In such situations, the ballistic and the forensic aspect is taken into account. In this report, it's missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we have any information as to how far they ran until Sanela was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have the exact information; however, judging by the position of the trench and the size of the building - the building is about 15 metres wide - and we don't know where exactly they were in Djure Jaksica Street, I suppose that they may have run for some 20 metres or so in total. But this is just an assumption. They were in Djure Jaksica Street, and in figure 81 it is on the right-hand side behind the building. Let me check if there is a better image where I could point to it -- no, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can assume that it was about 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the point of view of ballistics and from the point of view of establishing the intention of targeting these people, is it a fact that they were running of some importance?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it were possible to establish whether the testimony is true - and I can't be the judge of that - I just stated that one and the same person provided two different statements and I don't know which one's correct. I'm saying if it is true that they had been running and that they were shot before they reached the trench, then they were not shot from the Institute for the Blind. I suppose that there must have been an exchange of fire or a ricochet or something of that kind. And if they were on the border of the trench, as was shown in that video-clip, there is a theoretical possibility that the marksman was at the level of the ceiling in that room and that he opened fire from there. But this is another assumption and in my view it's very improbable that the marksman's position was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now this may not be a ballistics question. Is the vicinity of the trench of any importance? But you don't have to answer that. No.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have enough information. I don't know what was going on. We don't have a full picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can we look at F11 which is on page 131, paragraph 147 for the English version. Again, tell us what was said about this incident, and on the other hand what does the physical evidence show?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a complex incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up figure 90.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened on the 8th of October, 1994. According to the indictment, two trams were hit at the crossroads of Franje Rackog and Zmaja od Bosne Streets, and after that some passers-by were wounded. Something that surprised me as a layperson is the fact that in the footnote for this incident it is stated that one person was killed, whereas in the indictment, in the body of the indictment, it is stated that some persons were wounded. I'm -- I find it surprising that a dead person was mentioned only in the footnote. Unlike in the previous case, we had a lot of video material for this incident. There were a lot of statements as well; however, I have to say that we didn't have all the material that is available here in the court and it would have been of much use to us if we had had it at the time. However, we still managed to establish where that fire was opened from and how the events actually unfolded. According to our findings, the first tram number 206 was hit somewhere around the building of the Executive Council close to the containers that served as protection between the Executive Council building to the old tobacco factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which point denotes the place where tram 206 was hit.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the dotted line with an arrow and it is corrected with -- connected with a curve with two arrows that leads towards tram 206. Where it says "Tram 206," that's the place where the tram finally stopped, and you can see it in the video-clip that it is actually standing in front of that tobacco factory, 206.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What street is it in the place where the tram was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The projection of the point of impact across the river.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Vrbanja bridge and it is the street that leads towards the Vrbanja bridge. I believe that it was Djure Danica Street, but I really can't remember. The bridge here is the Vrbanja bridge. You can see the Assembly building and the Executive Council building as well. The first tram was hit somewhere around the place where it was passing in front of the Executive Council building, but it is not possible to say that with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first tram that was hit was 206?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and immediately after that tram 236 followed and it was hit approximately in the place which is depicted in the figure in front of the Executive Council building. And this was also recorded on the video-clip. Number 2 denotes the area in front of the Executive Council building and the School of Philosophy and that's where passers-by were shot as they were walking in the direction of the centre of the city. When they found themselves in that open area, a burst of fire was opened on them and television recorded that. That film I believe was shown in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about number 1?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 denotes the place where the tram was according to the police, a place across the road from Metaljka, the crossroads of Franje Rackog Street and Zmaja od Bosne Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the street south of number 1? What's its name?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its current name is Ferdo Hauptman Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was its main name?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was Djure Danica Street, if I remember it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you about the projection of number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about number 1?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is Franje Rackog Street which leads to the Metaljka building. This is the notorious crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And with respect to number 1, where is the so-called S-curve?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red line which encircles number 1 is at the beginning of that S-curve.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us what does it say in the reports? Where was the tram when it was hit and why are you claiming that it was hit in the projection of Djure Danica Street?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the reports, the tram was hit at the crossroads which is marked by number 1. We claim, however, that it was hit where it is marked as tram 236 and we claim that based on the video-clip and several witness statements provided by the people who were passengers on the trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to show a photo --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best proof of that is photo 92 and also 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can we look at page 135.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and the accused please be asked not to overlap and slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we should first look at 90 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, I take it, Mr. Karadzic, you noted the transcript. Because of overlapping, the interpreters didn't hear your entire -- your questions and answers. So page 135, we start over from there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, I notice that and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, could you please tell us what is the building in the background?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the background we can see the building of the Executive Council and the building that is a bit lower than that is the School of Philosophy, and here we see tram 236 standing next to the Executive Council building. The upper photo, number 92, depicts tram 236 and next to it we see a lot of shattered glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does that mean? Who took that photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That photo is a clip from the -- a still from the video-clip. There was a crew that was filming things as they unfolded, so it's a still from the video-clip. And what does it mean? The shattered glass on the street is the glass from the tram. Several witnesses confirmed that they heard a shot, the tram was hit, the glass was broken, and they started shouting to the driver, "Go on driving, go on driving." The driver, however, did not drive on. He stopped immediately, and here you can see that with respect to this broken window the tram moved for another metre or two which is probably the time that the driver needed to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now can we look at figure 95 which is on page 137.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another still from the film that was shown here, I believe, which depicts the passers-by being shot at as they were walking from the School of Philosophy towards the Executive Council building. The red ellipsoid shape points to a column of dust which was caused by the impact of the bullet on the soil. Based on that column of dust which is virtually vertical to the surface, we can conclude that the projectile had arrived at an acute angle of descent. If it had arrived at an angle of 2 or 3 degrees, that column of dust would be almost horizontal, it would follow the trajectory of the bullet. The second thing that can be discerned from this photo is the height of the column. On the left-hand side we can see an APC which is over 2 or even 2.5 metres high, and this column of dust is about the same height if not higher, which says that the energy of that bullet was really high and that the bullet was shot from -- for a relatively close range.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us about the building on the left-hand side. What is it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building on the left-hand side is the building of the School of Philosophy, and further down is the building of the Land Museum in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now take the electronic pen and make a projection of Djure Danica Street and Franje Rackog Street on both sides of the School of Philosophy and mark them with numbers 1 and 2 respectively.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franje Rackog Street goes in this direction between these two buildings and Djure Danica Street leads by the School of Philosophy. Franje Rackog will be number 1 and Djure Danica Street will be number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the street that the bullets travel along, to put it that way?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullets travel along Djure Danica Street, which is marked by number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is on the other side of the street in the projection of the School of Philosophy?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the other side of that street there is -- what do you mean? On what side? In the direction of the centre of the city? In the centre of the city as the tram tracks go further on is the Executive Council building and the Assembly building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 139.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And before that, I need your initial and the date.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3638, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we'll take a break for 15 minutes and resume at 14 past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please let us focus on incident F14 which is on page 149 in the Serbian version; in English it's part of paragraph 175. How is this incident presented and what were your findings and what were they based on?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This incident happened on the 23rd of November, 1994, when a tram was hit between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get image 103, please, on page 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to another version, the tram was hit at the intersection by the Metaljka building. It's the intersection of Franje Rackog Street and Zmaja od Bosne Street. The police found out that the tram was hit by one bullet and that two persons were injured in the process because the bullet fragmented. But immediately something illogical was noticed. They say that the bullet entered through a half-open window and fragmented in the process, but that's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on this image, please tell us where the impact on the tram happened.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is roughly the underlined spot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Wait for a moment. We would like to zoom in on the proper picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The pen.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the position of the tram according to the first version, that of the tram driver, because he said that the tram was at the switch toward the railroad station which is here. And the second position is based on the statement of a witness who was wounded then and she marked this spot, hereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record, the witness marked number 1 for the first point and marked number 2 for the second point. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what is in the projection from spot 1 toward Grbavica, that is which street, and what is in the projection of spot 2?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projection from 1 -- from spot 1 to Grbavica is a side-street which goes -- which runs between buildings 4 and 3. And in the projection of spot 2 there is Franje Rackog Street which runs toward the Metaljka building, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For the transcript you said that building 4 was the Land Museum and number 3 was the Museum of the Revolution and that the projection runs between these two buildings; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a side-street. I don't know if it has a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whose variant is number 1?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the version of the tram driver. He described in detail how he reached that conclusion. He said that he heard the shot when the tram was at the switch toward the railroad station which is to the right. There's the Marsal Tito barracks and the switch toward the railroad station is next to it. And position number 2 was described by a witness who was injured on that occasion and she thinks that's where the tram was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness said that the Marsal Tito barracks is marked 5 in this photograph and this was not recorded. Could you please mark the street that runs to the station.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is. I'll mark it 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did the police accept? Which version?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accepted version was that involving point 2, which means that the fire -- that the shot was fired from Metaljka. There are also these high-rise buildings marked by this dotted ellipse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you find out?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We established that it is impossible for a bullet to fragment after passing through an open window. It was claimed that the two fragments hit two different persons. It is also very important to say in what positions these two injured persons were and to describe the nature of their injuries. Based on their respective positions and the wounds on their bodies, we concluded that they couldn't be hit from the positions of the VRS because in that case they would have been hit in the shoulder, that would have been the entry wound, whereas the exit wound would have been elsewhere on their bodies; whereas in reality they were hit in the shoulder and the exit wound was in the upper arm. That is one -- in one of them. In the other, the exit wound is also in the shoulder. They were hit in the front part of their bodies and the exit wound was in the rear part, and the angle of descent was great. The angle of descent of a bullet fired from VRS positions couldn't have been like that because the distance is pretty great. The angle of descent would have been around 10 degrees depending where the shot was fired from, be it from these high-rise buildings, the white high-rise buildings, or the Metaljka building. In this case, the situation is the opposite. The only place from where they could have been hit in this manner is from the direction of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it in relation to buildings 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let this be 7 and the direction in this case is marked 8. As we can see here, this angle is relatively small relative to the axis of the tram. So if the bullet enters the body in the front part of the shoulder, it can exit in the rear part of the body. Certainly it couldn't have been in the upper arm. The differences between the exit wounds and the entry wounds according to the report is great in terms of height, and this points toward a great angle of descent, which indicates that it would have been the Executive Council from where the shot originated. And let me explain how the bullet could have fragmented without the police noticing. They didn't find out where the bullet entered the tram. The only possible place, taking into consideration the respective positions of the two persons, was the central pliable part, the joint of the tram. And the bullet may have hit something there that made it fragment and the police didn't notice that. But if the bullet was fired from the VRS positions on Grbavica, the bullet couldn't have hit this joint and then fragmented to hit the two persons, which means that the bullet could not have been fired from the VRS positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please date and initial this. And please mark the Executive Council with a number 9.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit D3639.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get image 104 on page 151.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who marked this photograph and who took it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was marked by Afeza Karacic, one of the two persons who were injured in that tram. She marked the approximate position of the tram with this red arrow, whereas position 05 probably refers to the incident in which Dzenana Sokolovic was hit. It's the position that she showed as hers in that video-clip. Number 5 has nothing to do with this incident, but the red arrow does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we consider this version, what would have been the trajectory of the bullet if it had come from the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Metaljka building is in this direction so let's draw this line, and the angle would have been somewhat smaller if the bullet came from the white high-rise building. But this place is not visible from those buildings. There was a photograph made for the Milosevic -- for the trial of General Milosevic and it shows that there is no optical visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please mark the line pointing to Metaljka with number 1 and the line pointing to the white high-rise buildings number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it possible for the bullet to have come from either of these directions?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I can also mark the position of one part of the tram, and I'll also indicate the joint of the tram. The persons were right here, right behind the joint and its bellows, as it were, and the projectile must have entered the tram in front of the joint in order to hit them; otherwise, it's impossible. I'll mark the joint with a number 3 and number 4 marks the tram. It's impossible for the bullet to hit the joint and the two persons sitting right behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please mark the trajectory as it must have been according to your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This must have been it next to the Faculty of Philosophy. It goes through the joint and hits the two persons, direction 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is on the other -- at the other end of this line?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Executive Council. The distance is relatively small from this point to the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the angle of descent and the angle of the trajectory match your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please date and initial this.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this -- just a second. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just for information, the unmarked original photograph was P116 in the Dragomir Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3640, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I believe that this original exhibit in Milosevic had this red arrow?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took that from the documents that we received. It has to do with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please focus on incident 15 now. The page number in Serbian is 154 and in the English version, paragraph 184. What did the police establish here, what was taken over by the indictment, and what were your findings?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This incident took place on the 25th of February, 1995, and a tram was hit with a burst of gun-fire, eight to ten bullets, and there was a total of ten traces. Eight bullets ended up in the panelling of the tram, four of which pierced the panelling and four remained in the panelling. On the same occasion a few persons were wounded. On the basis of the description provided by the police, it was noted that four projectiles ended up in the panelling of the tram, that is to say they had not pierced it. The police claimed that the projectiles had been fired from the white high-rise building in Grbavica. In respect of the position of the white high-rise buildings and the site of the incident, it can be noted that the angle of the trajectory in relation to the axis of the tram is almost 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see photograph number 106 on page 155. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this helpful in terms of what you have been saying?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, partly. This is the stop in front of the revolution -- of the Museum of the Revolution. According to the witness statements, the tram stopped there and then when it left - so it was 20 metres later or whatever - it was hit. The white high-rise buildings are opposite this museum, so obviously the tram stop cannot be seen from the white high-rise buildings. Obviously the tram either had to go further away where there was more visibility -- so the white high-rises are basically almost straight ahead. That shows that the angle is almost 90 degrees and that's what really matters here. So if this angle is almost 90 degrees and in view of the distance involved, the distance at which these white high-rise buildings are, and if we look at the height of the white high-rise buildings, the maximum angle of descent on the vertical plain could be about 10 degrees. Now, what does this mean specifically? That means that the bullet that hits the tram has an exit opening on the panelling only a few centimetres below that of the opening at the point of entry. That means, in other words, that a bullet that is fired from the white high-rise buildings cannot have such a trajectory; that is to say for the bullet to remain in the panelling, it has to pierce it 8 to 10 centimetres. There is metal there and then some other thermo-isolation material and then there is more -- there is another layer. Perhaps it is a plastic layer rather than metal, so that would not be a problem for the bullet to get through. Those bullets that remained in the panelling could not have been fired from the white high-rise buildings. The police compiled photo documentation on that occasion and their attention was focused on one trace only, that is number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see photograph 109 on page 158.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps 107 would be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Let's start with 107 then.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, let's. We see part of the tram in this photograph where the traces are marked, 1, 2, and 3. That is -- those are the entry points of these bullets from the burst of gun-fire consisting of ten bullets. The difference in height is very small, as you can see. It's about 30 centimetres. Had the burst been fired for -- from a distance of over 300 metres, as far off as the white high-rise buildings, the dispersion would have been far greater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And now we can note trace 3 that the police devoted particular attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we need to look at image 108?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, 108, so that we can see what it looks like from the inside. The police took a photograph of that place from the inside too and they established that trace 3 is at the same height as trace 3 is on the external side, which corresponds to what I was saying a moment ago; namely, that in that case the bullet had been fired from the white high-rise building because there is a very small difference in height between the exit and entry points, and that can be seen if you remember the position in the previous image. This is trace 3 as well and that's what the police wrote in the comment attached to this photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see image 109 now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in this image like in the previous one - and we'll explain it now - it is very easy to see the point above the radiator above the chair, projectile number 3 marked on the external side, not this thing up here. This trace 3 that the police marked as the exit point is a point, or rather, a dot that was marked using a marker pen, and that can be seen very nicely in this photograph; namely, the thickness of this arrow that was also marked using that same kind of marker is of the same thickness as this dot, obviously the colour and everything else. And there is no -- well, it doesn't look the way an exit point usually looks. The exit point opening is the one down here and we can see how big the difference is, and that indicates that this projectile also came at a large angle of descent, that is to say from very nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a circle around this and put, say, number 4 --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. This is the actual exit opening. That would be number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can deformities in the metal be seen at opening 4?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that can be noted and this is characteristic for an opening that is the result of a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The difference in height in their version, it's 2 millimetres. And what about here?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, the height difference would be between 20 and 25 centimetres. I established that -- I measured that. I measured the different heights in the tram, so it is with a high degree of certainty that I can claim that it is between 20 and 25 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is your ultimate conclusion, your final conclusion? These shots -- actually, first of all, the VRS, did it have sniper rifles that could fire bursts of gun-fire?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, this is not due to sniper fire. This is a classical burst of gun-fire, either from an automatic rifle or a machine-gun, it doesn't matter. According to all of these traces, obviously this was fired from some building nearby, that is to say from a short distance and a relatively considerable height. It could have been the Museum of the Revolution or the next building. I think it's a building that used to be the building of Union Invest. All of that is in this area of, say, 30 to 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at 3 and 4 now -- sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3641, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we briefly look at a series of photographs, 2, 3, and 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since you are familiar with weaponry and ammunition, can you tell us what these projectiles are shown in Van Lynden's film? And the Army of Republika Srpska, did it have anything that looked like this when fired? It's page 34 in Serbian and it's within paragraph -- paragraph 7, 7 in the English language. So images 2 and 3 -- oh, yes, we have it. Thank you. Can you describe this to us, what your findings are.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an excerpt from a film that shows some kind of bursts of gun-fire during the night. We see a lot of illuminated circles, a series of them, but there are others that do not follow the series. According to the number of these circles, one might conclude that this is a burst of gun-fire from some anti-aircraft gun, that is to say it could be 20 millimetres, 30, possibly 57. Ammunition for these artillery pieces does have a tracer that gives some light off and that is how one can follow its trajectory, correct fire, et cetera. Now, what is illogical in these photographs? It's the size of these illuminated circles. It exceeds, by far, the size of this illuminated trace that is left by bullets from an anti-aircraft gun. Also, this tracer looks like a comet, if you will, so it's elongated, especially if it's filmed on camera. Only if it is filmed from a very great distance, then it can look different. I think that this was taken relatively close up. I think that in image 3 you can see Mr. Lynden, you see his silhouette here, and that shows that this is -- there was no zoom used and that's important. 100 to 150 metres, these illuminated circles. Obviously this is not a trace that comes from anti-aircraft ammunition. What actual traces like that look like can be seen in another part of the film. You can see how the camera registers traces of a true anti-aircraft projectile; that is in image number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dynamically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. So image number 3 comes from where? Is that in our evidence, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency, Van Lynden admitted to us that he had edited this, although at first it had seemed that he was doing this live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you -- I'm asking you whether you have an exhibit number now for that and the time-frame for this frame?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's cited here, the film and the time, in footnotes 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think footnote 9 is for image 4, not image 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same film. If it's not cited --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we have footnote 8, but I don't know the exhibit number. I'll leave it at that. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we see image number 4, could you please tell us something about the dynamic behaviour of the tracer bullets in question?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dynamic behaviour of these projectiles is not typical of the anti-aircraft ammunition that I referred to because you can see with the naked eye that they move slowly. It depends on the cannon actually, but it is obvious that the cannons or the rhythm of these projectiles is much lower than of the true anti-aircraft projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see image number 2 and number 3 at the same time? And to be clear, could you mark what is noticeable from this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will mark this. This would be a burst from a one-barrelled cannon; however, at the far left end you can see that two tracer bullets overlap and that cannot be. The far left side --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark just one of them, and the second circle is below.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the next one?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The origin of this and those above it cannot be accounted for by the fire opened from this particular type of weapon. The two have nothing to do with each other. There are actually two or three illuminated objects that fly independently of each other and they cannot be linked to the burst of fire. They could not have been fired either from artillery or rocket weapons because we wouldn't be able to see them. The origin of these that I'm going to mark, I'm going to mark burst number 1, and one on the left-hand side will be 2, the one below it will be 3, and there will be 4, 5, and 6. And these last three ones have nothing whatsoever to do with the previous bursts of fire nor can their presence here be accounted for in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put today's date and sign this image. Can we see Van Lynden in the photo?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see his silhouette and I can trace the silhouette if that will be of any assistance to you. This photo shows that zoom was not used, so nobody can think that the circles are much larger on account of the zoom that was used because it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date and the initial, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3642, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we look at image 6, page 36, paragraph 7 for the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, we had to show figure number 4 to show --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, number 4, page 35, please.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you can actually notice things here. It may not be that easy. I'm going to try and -- I apologise. Look at this trace here and here. I believe that there's another one here. Yes. This is an anti-aircraft projectile with a tracer. And it was recorded at dusk and you can see clearly the light that it leaves behind. The camera lens is slower than the projectile itself. It makes 20 to 30 shots in a second, whereas the projectile is somewhat faster. So the trace seemed to be longer. It should look like a comet when photos are taken with a camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was this taken from?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a reference. Again, we're talking about Lynden's video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The date and the initial.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, Excellencies, and can we please look at the photo below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3643, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the Chamber will take a somewhat earlier break and we'll break for half an hour, resume at 1.35 -- oh, 11.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, the text is rather self-explanatory in terms of the two consecutive frames. Why did you choose them from Van Lynden's video?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can notice something illogical here. On the left-hand side, the last illuminated circle is small in comparison with the other three. At the next moment, and the photo is on the right-hand side, we can see that that that small circle all of a sudden is faster than a large circle and now it is third in a row instead of fourth in a row. And this is impossible when it comes to a burst of fire. A bullet that was fired later cannot reach its target sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the -- Mr. Karadzic's comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unless the projectile had been in training. That was the joke that I made. Thank you. I believe that everything else is self-explanatory from the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I would like to tender this report pursuant to Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton, any objection to the admission of the small arms fire report?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, I do, on a number of grounds, but I'll just focus on what I think is the prevailing one. One of the fundamental thresholds -- one of the most significant thresholds for the admission of an expert report is that the Trial Chamber should be able to rely on its -- to rely on it. So the report needs to be transparent; this is not. The report needs to be reliable; this is not. The report is far and away in many places outside of this witness's professed area of expertise. We've heard evidence over the last couple of days relating to statistics. We've heard evidence about horticulture. We've heard evidence relating to criminal investigations. We've heard legal evidence. And the probative value when you put all of those things together, Your Honour, is, in my submission, so low that the report is of no assistance to this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you reflect such objections in your response to the notice of expert evidence, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We did reflect in our submissions the fact that these matters -- any number of the items I have just cited were far and away outside of this witness's area of expertise. I could find, Your Honours, in a couple of moments the relevant citation in the footnote if that's of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And as a result of that objection, the Chamber ordered some redaction of the expert report .

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you are now objecting to the admission of the remainder of the report?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's without -- the assertions in the remainder of the report are without foundation, outside of the witness's area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. You've already ruled in your decision of the 12th of March, 2013, concerning matters that were outside of the witness's expertise. You've excluded those that you found necessary to exclude. You've noted that others which could not be conveniently excluded would be given appropriate weight by the Chamber. And I think that there's enough basis to admit the report and leave it to you to decide what weight to give to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having had the opportunity to hear the witness's evidence, the Chamber will consider the issue further and will give its ruling later on, in due course. Shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now I would like to call up 1D5600 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, would you please tell us what is this report, or rather, a comparative analysis that you drafted together with your associates who were your co-authors?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we worked on the numerous incidents of shelling, we observed that the two experts, Berko Zecevic and Richard Higgs, in their reports present some elements that we couldn't agree with in professional terms. We could not agree with the methodology of work that they employed. That's why we produced a separate document where we would provide our own opinion, if that would be of any use, because this shows why we do not agree with their methodology. Let me tell you briefly what our main objection to that methodology was. In terms of Berko Zecevic's findings, in a large number of cases he introduces an assumption based on which he then draws extensive conclusions without offering any sources for the claims that he presents. Let me just tell you briefly by way of example, when it comes to air bombs he introduces an assumption that they were produced without any documentation, that there were no conditions in place for their manufacture, that there were no firing tables, still they were fired, and so on and so forth. Our information was contrary to that, and in order to corroborate our information we provided some other cases that were eliminated from the report so that the report now does not bear the same weight that we originally wanted it to bear. If we had provided examples that would corroborate our claims, the case is similar with Mr. Higgs' report. He himself stated that his task was to review all of the cases and to verify the accuracy of the investigations that were carried out by the Sarajevo police. According to our opinion, he did not focus on verifying those investigations to the extent he should have done that. He explained some things in order to prove that the allegations by the police were correct. For example, in the incident that happened on the 22nd of January, 1994, he presented a claim, according to which the Serbian forces intentionally targeted children from the Institute for the Blind. They claimed that they had seen where the first shell had fallen and then they aimed their subsequent fire to the second group of children who were some 200 metres away from that place. In that he ignored the fact that the place of the incident was absolutely invisible to anybody who was standing at the positions by the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All these contradictions, have they been dealt with in this document?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were dealt with here and some there. We also wanted to show some other examples, but they ended up being redacted. So these examples have not made it into the report. Therefore, we do not have a complete picture that we wanted to present. Since these are not incidents from the indictment and in our view they were very characteristic, but they have been redacted which is why we wanted to provide an additional explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you study the incidents that have been eliminated from the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is your conclusion why they were eliminated? In other words, how would the analysis of those eliminated incidents reflect on your findings? Why are they striking, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the findings of Mr. Higgs, I would like to tackle the incident in Livanjska Street. In these proceedings that incident has been mentioned. UNPROFOR concluded that the shell had been fired from the BiH army positions. Mr. Higgs used a photo and based on that photo, while ignoring the distortion of the image, he established that UNPROFOR erroneously measured the size of the crater. And in that way, he proved that UNPROFOR had made a mistake and that the shell had been fired from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps the Defence will also analyse the eliminated incidents; however, you owe me -- or rather, I owe you a question about a sniping incident for which you said that the person who was killed in the incident found a place in the footnote, whereas the person who was wounded made it into the body of the indictment. Can you tell us whether you're familiar with the nature of the wound in the dead person?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That happened on the 8th of October. I believe that the incident number is F11. Let me just check to see if I'm right. Yes, F11. In the official report it is stated that that person, that that man, was killed and that the entry wound was on the right-hand side of his face, whereas the exit wound was on the left shoulder-blade. This points to the fact that the descent angle of the bullet that had been fired was large. However, when we drafted our report, we did not have a high-quality photo available to us and that is why we did not analyse the case for the purpose of our report, because we could not get confirmation that that description was indeed correct. In the month of February of this year, in the case of General Mladic, a witness, Edin Suljic, testified. He had been involved in the investigation of that incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I didn't realise for a moment we'd gone back to the small arms report, but now I see where this is going and the witness is referring to the testimony -- one of the two testimonies which was included in the 19 documents we were notified of late that I raised a very strong objection to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up the document and maybe then you can decide? 1D7474.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what -- I was just reading again what Mr. Poparic just has said. What does it have anything to do with his expertise? You can use material in your submission later on. Let's see where you are heading.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, the Defence is concerned about the blatant examples that are crucial for judgement have been eliminated from the indictment or have ended up in footnotes. I believe that we will ask from the expert to analyse all of the eliminated incidents which are -- exist in other indictments and they have been omitted from mine. We would like to know why they have been omitted, according to which pattern or model. But if you will, why don't we look at 1D7474. You don't have to admit it, but let's at least have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I think the Chamber made it clear the Chamber would not hear evidence from this witness with respect to the unscheduled or redacted incidents. I think we made it clear in our decision. I would like you to comply with that decision. So I'm not sure whether this has anything to do with it or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this incident was admitted and we are pointing at the footnote which was the main victim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- so are you talking about the F11 incident?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.
